papers.title: Abnormal inferior parietal hub configuration during mindfulness following rumination in remitted depression.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Rumination persists in remitted depression (RD) and increases relapse risk. Mindfulness-based strategies may interrupt rumination, but network reorganization during the transition from rumination to mindfulness is poorly understood. METHODS: Fifty-one patients with RD and 41 healthy controls (HCs) were recruited and completed a six-state fMRI paradigm (resting state I, negative autobiographical recall, rumination, mindfulness, distraction, and resting state II). We used network-based statistics (NBS) within each state and graph-theoretical analyses across sparsity thresholds. Rumination severity was assessed with the Ruminative Responses Scale (RRS). An exploratory analysis tested rumination to the mindfulness similarity of the left inferior parietal lobule (IPL) connectivity profile. RESULTS: During mindfulness, RD showed a hyperconnected NBS component linking default mode, dorsal and ventral attention, and frontoparietal and somatomotor networks, anchored in a left IPL hub. A more widespread hyperconnected component was observed during resting state II in RD. Graph theoretical analyses showed that, during mindfulness, RD exhibited reduced degree centrality, betweenness centrality, and nodal efficiency in the left IPL (all FDR-corrected  CONCLUSIONS: RD is characterized by an IPL-centered hub configuration during mindfulness following rumination, marked by broad coupling but reduced hub efficiency and reduced rumination-to-mindfulness reconfiguration. Clinically, inefficient hub reconfiguration during mindfulness attempts may index a residual vulnerability and may represent a candidate target for monitoring and intervention.

papers.title: Ketamine, an interoceptive associative agent? Evidence from ketamine-assisted Mindfulness-Oriented Recovery Enhancement for opioid use disorder.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Relapse in opioid use disorder (OUD) remains common despite pharmacotherapy. Altered interoceptive processing may contribute to addiction, and ketamine-induced changes in salience and insula-related networks may facilitate mindfulness-based interoceptive learning. AIMS: This secondary analysis examined whether ketamine-assisted psychotherapy (KAP) added to Mindfulness-Oriented Recovery Enhancement (MORE) improved interoceptive awareness and whether these changes mediated reductions in opioid craving. METHODS: Sixty-eight adults with OUD receiving buprenorphine were randomized to 8 weeks of MORE with or without KAP. Assignment was unblinded, and outcomes were self-reported. Interoception was assessed using ecological momentary assessment (EMA) of body awareness and Multidimensional Assessment of Interoceptive Awareness (MAIA) subscales. Posttreatment EMA data were available for 18 MORE + KAP and 15 MORE participants. Mixed-effects models and path analysis were conducted. RESULTS: Piecewise modeling showed a greater increase in EMA-assessed body awareness salience in MORE + KAP during days 1-35, spanning the pre-dosing and first-ketamine-dose period ( CONCLUSIONS: Adjunctive ketamine was associated with rapid, sustained increases in body awareness salience. Improvements in interoceptive regulatory capacity mediated reduced opioid craving, supporting interoception as a potential mechanism and treatment target in ketamine-augmented mindfulness interventions for OUD. papers.title: Interventions to promote teachers' mental health in the workplace: a scoping review.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To map the scientific evidence on interventions aimed at promoting teachers' mental health, including an analysis of their characteristics, measured outcomes, results and limitations. METHOD: A scoping review was conducted across seven data sources and grey literature, in accordance with the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodology and the PRISMA-ScR guidelines. The search was performed in August 2024 and updated in August 2025. Primary intervention studies employing experimental or quasi-experimental designs were included, with no restrictions on language or year of publication. The final sample comprised 15 publications. RESULTS: The studies were published between 1990 and 2022, and were conducted in high-income countries. Most of the studies employed quasi-experimental designs (n = 9; 60.0%) and focused on worker-directed interventions (n = 13; 86.6%), particularly mindfulness-based approaches (n = 5; 38.4%). The most frequently assessed outcomes were related to mental ill health (n = 12), primarily stress, burnout, anxiety and depression. Indicators of mental health promotion were assessed less frequently and generally treated as secondary outcomes. The main limitations included the absence of control groups, small sample sizes, reliance on self-reported measures and lack of longitudinal follow-up. CONCLUSION: The available evidence predominantly focused on worker-directed interventions with an emphasis on reducing symptoms. Positive mental health indicators were generally considered secondary outcomes, suggesting an approach oriented towards managing mental ill health rather than promoting mental health.

papers.title: Spiritual self-care practice and mindfulness among patients with cancer: A cross-sectional study - EXPRESSION OF CONCERN.
Trait and daily self-compassion in relation to daily stress, eating behaviours and sleep: a daily diary study.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Trait self-compassion is consistently associated with reduced stress and health-promoting behaviours. This study examined whether trait and state-like daily self-compassion played similar roles in relation to daily stress and health behaviours, and whether they moderated the associations between daily stress and daily health behaviours. METHODS: A sample of 138 individuals completed baseline measures of trait self-compassion and eating styles, followed by a 7-day daily diary in which daily self-compassion, stress, eating, and sleep were assessed. RESULTS: Trait self-compassion was found to be positively associated with daily self-compassion. Trait self-compassion was also associated with uncontrolled, emotional, and intuitive eating styles. Multilevel modelling indicated that trait self-compassion was related to lower daily total snacking and better sleep outcomes, including reduced pre-sleep arousal and morning tiredness. At a daily level, self-compassion was associated with greater vegetable consumption, fewer hassles, more uplifts but poorer sleep quality. Finally, trait self-compassion moderated the relationship between daily stress and total snacking, such that individuals higher in self-compassion reported less snacking on stressful days. CONCLUSIONS: These findings extend existing knowledge by highlighting distinct associations of trait and daily self-compassion with daily stress, eating behaviours and sleep, and suggest that future research should further examine their potential roles in daily stress-health behaviour processes.
